title: Residential Natural Gas Supply Thermostat Shipment — Questions Answered
content:
**When does the smart thermostat included with a Residential Natural Gas Supply plan ship?**
On a plan that includes a thermostat, the thermostat ships once the agreement's completed billing cycles reach the plan's ship point (the number of completed cycles after which the included thermostat ships).

**What counts as a completed billing cycle?**
Counting from the agreement's service start date up to the handling date, the completed cycles are the number of distinct billing-cycle start dates among the agreement's energy charge lines whose billing period ends on or before the handling date. A cycle still running on the handling date is not completed.

**Does the agreement's status matter?**
Yes. The thermostat ships only while the agreement is active, as the agreement's status in the company's records shows. An agreement in any other status is not shipped a thermostat.

**Can one agreement receive two thermostats?**
No. An agreement receives at most one thermostat, so its thermostat ship date is written once and never changed.

**Does a plan change or a renewal into a thermostat plan ship one?**
No. A plan change or renewal into a thermostat plan does not ship a thermostat; only a new enrollment on such a plan does.

### Worked illustration (hypothetical dates)

An agreement on a plan whose ship point is 2 completed cycles started supply on 10 January. Its energy lines cover cycles starting 10 January (ending 9 February) and 10 February (ending 9 March). On 5 March only the first cycle has ended, so 1 cycle is completed and no thermostat ships. On 12 March both cycles have ended: 2 cycles are completed, and if the agreement is active the thermostat ships.
